Water and electricity

Assumptions

change any value; the gut and village figures update

Every value here comes from an open source. Rain is no longer a guess: monthly rainfall at Loni from Open-Meteo (ERA5, 2018–2026)20 gives effective rain month by month with the FAO formula (Pe = 0.8P − 25 above 75 mm/month, else 0.6P − 10)21, and irrigation need is summed month by month per plot. Application efficiency: FAO indicative values, 60% surface, 90% drip22; banana and pomegranate plots use drip, the rest surface. Wire-to-water efficiency: existing farm pumpsets run at 20–35% (BEE)23; 30% is used. Head: pre-monsoon water levels in Indapur are 10–20 m and borewells draw from 50–180 m12. Norm: 1,192 kWh/HP/yr, latest MERC-approved10. Cost of supply: ₹4.83/kWh, MSEDCL's agricultural cost of supply for FY 2026-27 in its tariff petition (not yet the approved figure)24. Farmers with pumps up to 7.5 HP pay nothing under the Baliraja scheme (Apr 2024 to Mar 2029)11; the state carries the cost.

How the numbers are made

  1. Crops per plot. Plots come from the October 2026 drone segmentation. Each crop cycle is labelled by matching its NDVI-derived Kc curve to published curves, and 26 cycles carry a field-photo label18. Most labels are uncertain, which is why weak matches are faded.
  2. Water use. ET = Kc × ETo, with Kc = 1.457 × NDVI − 0.1725 (clamped 0.15–1.25) and ETo from ERA5 0.25° via Open-Meteo (FAO-56 Penman–Monteith)18, summed over every 5-day step of the water year, fallow included.
  3. Irrigation need = max(0, ET − effective rain) ÷ application efficiency. Canal and tank water is not separated, so this is the total irrigation the crops needed, from any source.
  4. Electricity = need × 9.81 × head ÷ (3,600 × wire-to-water efficiency), in kWh per m³. Pump-hours = kWh ÷ (HP × 0.746).
  5. Value. Harvested area × yield × price. Cane price is FRP adjusted for recovery (₹3.56/q per 0.1% above or below 10.25%), minus harvest and transport58.
